value: Simulates resource development, not full games (no interaction, no removal).
Draw every turn including turn 1 (multiplayer Commander).
Mulligan: keep 7-card hands with 2-5 lands; up to 2 fresh redraws, keep the last.
One land drop per turn when available.

LANDS ENTER UNTAPPED, ALWAYS, and the one in hand longest is the one played. A tapland costs nothing here and no land is ever chosen over another, so this model CANNOT rank two lands that make the same colours — `mana-analysis` and `mana-fit` are what answer a land question, and they are deterministic for exactly this reason.
Mana rocks ('{T}: Add') contribute from the turn after they are cast.
Commander cast on first affordable turn (highest spending priority).
Bodies count = creatures cast + tokens parsed from 'create ... token' text.
Target assembly counts cards DRAWN by a turn (cast cards still count).

X-SPELL DRAW IS PAID FOR OUT OF WHAT IS LEFT. An {X} instant or sorcery that draws X is cast AFTER every other loop has spent what it wanted, with the whole remaining pool, and only when X would be at least 2 — a pilot does not cast Stroke of Genius for one card, and every cheapest-first loop in this module would have, because Scryfall counts {X} as zero and the card's `cmc` is only its fixed part. That floor is the one authored number in this channel. Casting last makes the figure a FLOOR in the other direction too: the spell only ever gets mana nothing else asked for. Corpus sweep: 33 X-cost instants and sorceries that draw X, 28 credited and 5 skipped — a split card whose cmc is both halves, an alternative cost under which X is 0, and three whose X is bounded by a discard or by a graveyard this model does not have.

CARD DRAW IS ONE A TURN UNLESS `model_draw` IS SET. With the flag on, four channels are modelled — a card's own ETB draw, an instant or sorcery that draws, an upkeep trigger, and an ARRIVAL trigger that draws when other creatures or tokens enter (Welcoming Vampire, Caretaker's Talent), which rides the same single door the ETB damage payoffs use. Activated draw (needs a spending policy this model has no opinion on), X-based draw (board-dependent), and death- or attack-triggered draw (no deaths, and attacks only under `model_combat`) are NOT modelled and the cards are named in `meta.card_advantage.draw_not_modelled`. A conditional trigger — 'if you control an artifact', 'you may draw' — is treated as unmodelled rather than assumed to be on: 39 of the 348 ETB-draw cards in the corpus carry one.

AN ARRIVAL-DRAW ENGINE NEVER SEES ITS OWN ARRIVAL. Welcoming Vampire is a 2/3 that draws 'whenever one or more OTHER creatures you control with power 2 or less enter'; registered before its own entry it passed its own gate and drew a card it does not draw, overstating edgar-vampires by 22% at turn eight. The deferral applies to every card and not only the ones worded 'other', which understates Tocasia's Welcome and two relatives by one draw on the turn they land.

ARRIVAL DRAW IS SMALLER WITHOUT `model_combat`, and legitimately so. The channel rides the one door onto the battlefield, which `model_combat` also uses to spawn token copies and ETB-payoff tokens — those are real additional arrivals that do not exist in the resource-only model. Measured on edgar-vampires: 1.264 extra cards by turn ten with both flags against 1.106 with draw alone. Before 2026-08-28 the gap was 1.264 against 0.323, because every call to that door sat inside `if model_combat:` and a draw-only deck silently lost three quarters of its arrival draws.

HELD-UP INTERACTION is reported as two series and both are FLOORS. This model casts everything it can afford every turn, so `interaction_castable` is what a pilot developing at full speed has left over, not what a pilot choosing to hold up two mana would have. A low figure is therefore a real finding and a high one is unambiguous good news.

Tutors are modeled as wildcards: a CAST tutor that fetches to hand or the top — including a TYPED one (Worldly Tutor, Sarkhan's Triumph), which the old literal 'a card' match missed entirely — fills ONE missing any_of group. Consumed once, mana paid, and a tutor that puts the card on top of the library costs a turn. An ACTIVATED, ETB or death-triggered tutor does not count, because this model only knows 'drawn and affordable'; nor does a land fetch, which is ramp and has no channel here yet. Reported as the *_assisted figures; the unassisted figures beside them exclude tutors entirely.

ENTERS-THE-BATTLEFIELD PAYOFFS are modelled: damage equal to the entering creature's power (Terror of the Peaks), X damage where X counts your board (Scourge of Valkas, Dragon Tempest), a token (Lathliss) and a token COPY of what entered (Miirym). Every arrival fires them — cast, token or copy — and a copy is itself an arrival, so they compound, which is the deck working rather than a bug. A payoff worded 'another NONTOKEN' does not re-trigger on its own tokens, which is the brake the rules already had. A chain is capped at 12 deep. X counts the whole board rather than one subtype: exact where the creatures are Dragons, generous otherwise.

The COMMANDER joins the battlefield when cast, attacks, and fires its own triggers. It used to be a mana sink and a flag — cast, then dropped — so a 10/10 flier contributed no power and never swung. Commander tax, death and recasting are still not modelled: it is cast once and it stays.

STATIC cost reduction IS modeled: a commander's eminence from the command zone (live from turn one, unremovable) and typed reducers once they are on the battlefield. It pays GENERIC only and is floored at the coloured pip count, because a discount can never pay a pip. A reduction that SCALES with a board state (Animar, Rakdos, Hamza) is refused rather than counted flat, and cost reduction on artifacts, noncreature spells or a colour is not modeled at all.
Rituals are not modeled (conservative).

Extra card draw is NOT modeled: one card per turn, always. That understates every deck, but by an amount proportional to how much draw it runs — so it is conservative WITHIN a deck and not neutral BETWEEN them. `meta.card_advantage` reports how much of each list this hides. Card advantage is measured nowhere in this suite.

Treasures are a one-shot STOCKPILE, not a mana rock: spent only when lands and rocks fall short, and gone once broken. Reported separately from mean_available_mana_by_turn, which still means repeatable mana per turn.

Only Treasure triggers a goldfish can see are modeled — upkeep and landfall are RECURRING, Saga chapters likewise; a `cast` or enters-the-battlefield trigger pays out ONCE, when its own source resolves. Combat- and opponent-gated sources produce NOTHING here, because this model has no combat and no opponents; they are named in meta.treasure_sources_not_modelled so a low hoard figure is legible.

COMBAT: one opponent at 40 life who does nothing — no blockers, no removal, no interaction. This is a goldfish in the literal sense, so `kill_turn` is the turn an UNOPPOSED board would finish ONE seat, not a win rate.

Attacks with every creature that is not summoning-sick; haste is read from the ORACLE TEXT (this line said 'type line' and was simply wrong). There is nothing to block, so nothing is ever held back — in a real four-player game you would keep blockers, which makes this an optimistic clock and a pessimistic board.

TEAM HASTE IS MODELLED (2026-09-11). A permanent that says 'creatures you control have haste' lets every creature attack the turn it lands, from the turn the grant itself lands; a typed grant (Karrthus: Dragons) reads the creature's type line; Dragon Tempest's grant reads keyword flying; riot is read as always choosing haste. TOKENS carry no type line and no flying here, so a typed or flying grant does not reach them. NOT read: a grant from the graveyard (Anger), an activated one (Crashing Drawbridge), one conditional on the board ('as long as'), and the lands whose mana carries haste (Hall of the Bandit Lord, Arena of Glory) -- this model taps no particular land. Before this a granted creature waited a turn and its haste enabler was read as nothing.

Attack triggers, combat-damage triggers and additional combat phases are modelled, which is what makes Treasure sources gated on combat produce here when they produce nothing without this flag. Effects the parser cannot read are named in meta.combat_effects_not_modelled.

DAMAGE MULTIPLICATION is modelled and stacks MULTIPLICATIVELY as the rules do: doubling the power, swinging twice and doubling the damage dealt is eight times, not four. Three wordings are read — a replacement effect on damage you deal (Twinflame Tyrant), a granted double strike (Atarka) and a power doubling (Thrakkus). A grant worded 'each Dragon you control' is treated as applying to the WHOLE team: exact in a deck whose attackers are Dragons, generous in one where they are not. A creature's own double strike multiplies only itself. Board power is unaffected — a double-striker is not a bigger creature.
Bodies count CREATURES only under this flag. Without it a Treasure token scores as a creature, which inflates `mean_bodies_by_turn` for any deck that makes non-creature tokens.

LIFE LOSS ON ARRIVAL COUNTS AS DAMAGE. 'Each opponent loses 1 life' (Corpse Knight) and 'deals 1 damage to each opponent' (Impact Tremors) are the same event, the same cadence and the same number against one opponent at 40 life, and only the second was priced until 2026-08-28. They are NOT the same in the rules — lifelink, damage prevention and 'whenever an opponent loses life' all separate them — and this model has none of those. Nine corpus cards read through this channel, plus Mirkwood Bats through a token-creation channel of its own.

DEATH-TRIGGERED DRAIN IS NOT MODELLED AND IS THE LARGEST KNOWN GAP HERE. Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant, Zulaport Cutthroat, Bastion of Remembrance and Elas il-Kor all key on a creature DYING, and nothing dies in this model: no blockers, no removal, no sacrifice outlets. Their contribution is ABSENT, not zero, and a deck whose kill runs through them is understated here by however much that line is worth. `simulate` against a real pod is where that number lives.

engine_health.why: the engine is online by turn 5 in 40% of 10,000 seeded games

engine.thesis: A five-colour Dragon deck that buys its own curve down with five cost reducers, then multiplies each arrival twice over — once into more bodies and triggers, once into doubled damage — and whose kill is proven on a board and still unproven as a board it can reach.

diagnosis.verdict: Above the mana line this deck is in good shape and the pilot is right about it; below the line it is five lands short of the corpus's 36–38 — and the table corroborates the KIND of claim without pricing the number, because a 100-game correlation between resource development and winning sets no land count. open_questions[2] routes that half to the goldfish. In 100 seeded Forge games against the pilot's pod it won 12 — 0.12, ci95 [0.070, 0.198], n=100 — and made 5.48 land drops a game (ci95 [5.15, 5.81], n=100), and inside that sample what separates its wins from its losses is RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT — land drops and the casts they buy. Sweeping all eighteen numeric per-seat fields the record keeps per game, the partition is NINE separating with a Welch interval excluding zero, EIGHT null, and ONE untestable — `eliminated_turn`, which cannot separate wins from losses even in principle because a winner is never eliminated (all twelve wins carry null). Exactly two of the nine are resource counts rather than consequences of having won: land drops (7.25 against 5.24, diff 2.01, ci95 [0.52, 3.50], p 0.0002) and casts (15.92 against 9.02, diff 6.89, ci95 [2.28, 11.51], p 0.0001). The other seven are downstream. First-attack timing is one of the eight nulls; turns survived is null too but is a quantity I derived, not a field the record keeps. Both nulls this document previously enumerated are non-resource, which is why 'land drops' alone read as exclusive when it was not. lean_into[3] decides whether the two are one finding or two and shows the working — all of it under Forge's own caveat that its AI is "best with aggro and midrange decks, poor to ok in control decks, pretty bad for most combo decks" and that every seat including ours is that AI. The binding axis is mana-base, 31 land copies against a 36–38 floor, with land drops falling 0.834 / 0.670 / 0.525 across turns three to five while 26 maindeck nonland entries cost five or more. The conversion above it is better evidenced than it has ever been: four presentable checker-passed stacks now rather than three, and stack 002's annotation establishes that the deck CAN kill a fresh 40-life seat — the claim this document previously carried the other way round.

latest.prompt: The pilot's log (5 games, 1W 4L, all debriefed) reads: mana was the loss twice (Blood Moon, closed by the pilot's decision; no green source, a mulligan rule), and the TELEGRAPH was the loss three times -- 'I ramped fast enough to broadcast the win before I could present lethal', 'the treasure pile plus fireballing every ETB made me the obvious problem', 'I pour it into the board too early and telegraph'. His verdict: 'speed without protection or politics makes me the obvious kill target before I can close', and after the refactor 'I now have zero responses' (no counterspells; protection is Swat, Teferi's, Heroic Intervention, Boros Charm, Greaves). His four research asks, verbatim: (a) dragons that grant haste to the board -- 'the problem is speed, not size'; (b) haste enablers generally -- 'Terror has to swing the turn it lands, not sit'; (c) protection density -- 'some lock-down (equipment indestructible?) that does not cost me dragon slots'; (d) dragons with ETB counters or flash, and protection on dragons or dragon enchantments, without slowing the deck down. Measured: Forge at standard-v3 0.353 [0.215, 0.521] over 40 games, engine played, piloting comparable, killed by combat damage at mean global turn 35, the commander resolved in 57% of games at global turn 27; the goldfish reads kill_by_8 0.79 and the commander cast by t6 only 33% (mean t6.9), 4 of 22 Dragons have haste; the audit reads card-advantage 4 (target 10), colour-sources -12 on the worst colour, interaction-breadth 4 of 5, ramp 22 (over), protection 8 (over by count but not by the pilot's read). What changes make this deck close faster than the table can converge on it -- haste so the dragons swing the turn they land, protection that does not cost dragon slots, responses -- and which of those does the evidence support, with every add named against the axis it closes and every cut priced? Ownership is not a constraint. No two-card infinites.

open_questions.question: Do Twinflame Tyrant and Solphim, Mayhem Dominus both apply to the same damage event — a Dragon Tempest or Terror of the Peaks trigger aimed at an opponent — for four times the printed damage, and if so, who chooses the order the two replacement effects apply in (CR 616.1)? Resolve on a board with one doubler, then both, and state the multiplier exactly.

Ganax, Astral Hunter under Miirym and Panharmonicon: does a TOKEN Dragon copy entering trigger Ganax's 'Whenever Ganax or another Dragon you control enters, create a Treasure token', and does Panharmonicon double that trigger? Resolve on stack 002's own board with Ganax added and state the Treasure count.

Stack 001 kills every opponent on its board, but that board assumes Ancient Gold Dragon has already connected in combat, and its d20 needs 12 or better rather than the 15 the scenario fixes. Build the REACHABLE version of THE ENTRY KILL — one of Dragon Tempest / Terror of the Peaks / Scourge of Valkas, one widener, one nontoken Dragon cast — and resolve whether the cascade reaches three opponents at 40 or state the exact shortfall, as 002 does at 64 against 72. Do not let it assume Panharmonicon: 007 measured that board without it at 20 damage, which kills nobody.

Hellkite Courser's enters-the-battlefield trigger, one domain and three sub-questions: does it put The Ur-Dragon onto the battlefield from the command zone, does the haste it grants make an attack legal that turn, and does the return to the command zone at the beginning of the next end step add nothing to the commander tax under CR 903.8?

Scourge of the Throne, alone: does its 'attacks for the first time each turn' dethrone-conditioned trigger untap all attacking creatures and grant an additional combat phase, and is 'the player with the most life' re-evaluated in that second combat against life totals the first combat has already changed? Then, given a second combat, do Utvara Hellkite's per-attacking-Dragon token trigger, Thrakkus's power doubling and Atarka's double strike each fire again on the re-declared attackers?

Re-run the goldfish with THE COMBAT KILL's multiplier leg widened from two cards to three (adding Twinflame Tyrant, whose doubling covers combat damage to an opponent) and report the assembled / by-turn-six / mean-turn deltas against the tracked 0.243 / 0.157 / 4.866. Report the counterfactual as a counterfactual; do not overwrite the tracked figures.

Does anything in the current 99 make its own creatures die on purpose, and if not, what are Atsushi's death trigger and Gadrak's end-step Treasure trigger actually worth? Measure how often each fires in a seeded run rather than assuming they are dead text.

Stack 001 fixes its d20 at 15 for determinism. What is the LOWEST roll that still kills the 30-life seat on that exact board, and the lowest that also kills the 38-life seat — and therefore what fraction of the twenty faces clears each bar? Resolve 001's board with the roll unfixed and report the thresholds.

THE ENTRY KILL's damage leg is three cards — Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas — at 19.9% of openers, and deck-audit flags it thin. Is three enough for the deck's best-evidenced kill, and what in the pool or the format would join that leg? Re-measure with a widened leg against today's 0.240 assembled / 0.153 by turn six.

Re-goldfish the swapped list (31 lands to 36, five untapped or flexible sources in, five spells and one eight-drop out) and report mean available mana at turn five (4.219 today), the turn-four and turn-five land-drop rates (0.670 / 0.525), and commander cast by turn six (0.041). Does five lands move them, and by how much?

What does the literature say about the floor on basic-land count for a five-colour Commander deck running Farseek, Nature's Lore, Skyshroud Claim, Encroaching Dragonstorm and Fabled Passage — and running Prismatic Vista alongside them, as this diagnosis prescribes — at what point does whiff risk become material, and how does that trade against generic fixing?

THE COMBAT KILL is declared at 0.204 assembled / 0.128 by turn six on a two-card multiplier leg (Atarka, World Render and Thrakkus the Butcher) and has no passing stack at all. Resolve one board: an attacking Dragon under Thrakkus or Atarka, against a 40-life seat with a plausible blocker — is it lethal, and does Scourge of the Throne's additional combat phase belong in that leg as a third member?

Fund the four-card cost-reducer component and re-measure. Add a fifth and a sixth reducer to `goldfish_targets.json`'s 'Cost reducer drawn' group — Morophon, the Boundless and Goreclaw, Terror of Qal Sisma are the two this diagnosis's engine block names as closers — and report what moves: the group's assembled and by-turn-six rates (0.518 / 0.419 today), the crossed 'Reducer + ramp assembled' target (0.417 / 0.285), commander cast by turn six (0.041) and mean available mana at turn five (4.219). Run it beside the five-land swap of open_questions[2] as well as instead of it, because the two buy the same turn by different routes.

Re-simulate against the same pod at a sample large enough to resolve the residual test in lean_into[3]: deck-skeptic sizes it at roughly 24 wins to settle whether casts carries signal independent of land drops, and roughly 48 to settle the reverse — about 200 and about 400 games at this deck's measured 0.12 win rate. Report the same eighteen-field sweep and the two OLS residuals.

Audit the mana base holistically for a five-colour dragon deck: is 9 basics the right count against the deck's land tutors, does the pip spread across the 22 nonbasic lands match what the dragons actually demand rather than being generic fixing, and are the 14 enters-tapped lands (5 always tapped) costing tempo where an untapped source would do? Black is the specific soft spot — 22% on-curve from lands alone, lowest of five colours, with no Swamp in the 99.

For a five-colour Commander deck with land tutors, what does the literature say about the floor on basic-land count — how many basics a Farseek/Nature's Lore/Skyshroud Claim package needs before whiff risk becomes material, and how that trades against generic fixing?

If land count and the ramp package were reshaped toward more untapped sources, how much would mean available mana by turn five (currently 4.219) and the commander cast rate (currently 4.1% by turn six, mean cast turn 8.172, never cast by turn ten in 7,170 of 10,000 iterations) actually move?

Which line, if any, is this deck's win line now? Three checker-passed stacks describe boards v1.0.0 can no longer make (003, 004, 006, all marked presentable: false) and the three that remain — 001 Dragon Tempest + Ancient Gold Dragon, 002 Miirym under Panharmonicon, 005 Sneak Attack — are not a proven kill.

The deck 'generates no value on the way down' against a pod that plays heavy creature removal and heavy board wipes — is that a real gap in the 99, and what would close it without costing dragon slots?
Is 'three to five lands behind curve' still true on the current list? The claim was made on the raised-land-base version, before the mana density shifted toward dorks and rocks.
Which dragons grant haste to the board, and which haste enablers fit a five-colour dragon curve, so that a dragon swings the turn it lands rather than sitting through a rotation of removal?
What protection density can this deck carry — the pilot floats lock-down such as equipment granting indestructible — without spending dragon slots?
What does a table-politics layer for a deck that visibly presents the biggest board look like — threat management, alliance timing, and when to hold a swing back?

Steven 'flew under the radar with his tap/untap engine and won it' while the table spent its removal on the pilot — does this deck have any way to interact with an opponent who assembles quietly, or is its only answer to be faster than him?
How often does a keepable opening hand for this deck contain no green source? The pilot proposes the mulligan rule 'no green source, consider shipping it' and it needs a rate before it becomes one.

Firespitter Whelp with Twinflame Tyrant and Panharmonicon alongside Terror of the Peaks: how much damage does one nontoken dragon arrival actually deal, and how does the doubling interact with the extra trigger?

The refactor removed every counterspell and the pilot reports 'zero responses'. What responses — dragons with ETB counters or flash, or protection on dragons or dragon enchantments — fit without slowing the deck down?

Across 003, 004 and 005 the pilot presents a board the table can read before he can close. Is the gap between broadcasting a threat and presenting lethal a property of this list — ramp-heavy, protection-thin, no haste — or purely a deployment habit the handbook should fix?

piloting.reading: our seat was handled about as well as the pod, so an A/B between two of your own lists against this table is played equally badly on both sides and remains informative. It is still not a claim about how the deck plays in your hands.

engine_casts.reading: the AI played the deck's declared engine; a win rate from this run is about the deck.
